decisive_items: Revealed a patent foramen ovale measuring 7.34 mm in width with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt on colour flow mapping
The patient was initially acyanotic from 2010 to 2016, but gradually became cyanotic after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis
Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 55 mmHg in 2021
response.rationale: Eisenmenger syndrome best explains the combination of a PFO with right-to-left shunt, pulmonary hypertension, and the clinical progression from acyanotic to cyanotic. The PFO alone (R7) is the anatomical defect but not the full syndrome; other candidates are either too broad (pulmonary hypertension) or contradicted (CTEPH) or secondary findings (tricuspid regurgitation).

rejected.why: Identifies the PFO but misses the pulmonary hypertension and cyanotic progression that define Eisenmenger syndrome.
Tricuspid regurgitation is a consequence of right heart strain, not the primary diagnosis.
Idiopathic PAH does not explain the PFO with right-to-left shunt or the cyanosis.
Pulmonary hypertension is a feature but not the specific syndrome; lacks the shunt and cyanosis.
CTEPH is contradicted by pulmonary angiography showing no embolism or fistulae.
Pulmonary arterial hypertension is too broad and does not account for the PFO shunt and cyanosis.
